title: Coefficient-square coherence of normalized sheaf Hom chain maps
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, and let $R,S,R',S'$ be sheaves of commutative rings, with maps $\varphi:R\to S$, $a:R\to R'$, $b:S\to S'$, $\varphi':R'\to S'$ satisfying $b\varphi=\varphi'a$. Use module sheaves, ordinary sheafified tensor, restriction, and actual unbounded product Hom complexes $H_R,H_S,H_{R'},H_{S'}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] [def-pur-hom-complex]. Put $E=E_\varphi$, $A=E_a$, $B=E_b$, $E'=E_{\varphi'}$ for termwise ordinary scalar extension, and $U=U_\varphi$, $U'=U_{\varphi'}$ for restriction. Put $T_\psi(X)=\operatorname{Res}_\psi(\text{target ring of }\psi)\otimes_{\text{source ring of }\psi}X$.
Suppose for each of these ring maps and their composites we are given the chain maps of [lem-sfb-slice-scalar-hom-chain-adjunction] [lem-sfb-scalar-hom-chain-evaluation], normalized on every slice by
$$\nu_\psi(s\otimes x)=s\otimes x,\quad\theta_\psi(g)(p)=g(1\otimes p),\quad\alpha_\psi(s\otimes f)(p)=s\otimes f(p),\quad\sigma^\psi_q(s\otimes f)(t\otimes p)=stq(1\otimes f(p)).$$
These are statements about the actual product coordinates and identity-of-slice evaluations; pure tensors are sheafification-unit images [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Write $\chi_\psi(P,J)=\sigma^\psi_{\mathrm{id}_{E_\psi J}}:E_\psi H(P,J)\to H(E_\psi P,E_\psi J)$.
There exist natural chain isomorphisms $\kappa_X:BEX\xrightarrow{\sim}E'AX$ and natural chain maps $\mu_N:AUN\to U'BN$, $\tau_X:AT_\varphi X\to T_{\varphi'}AX$, with formulas
$$\kappa_X(s'\otimes(s\otimes x))=s'b(s)\otimes(1\otimes x),\quad\kappa_X^{-1}(s'\otimes(r'\otimes x))=s'\varphi'(r')\otimes(1\otimes x),$$
$$\mu_N(r'\otimes z)=\varphi'(r')\otimes z,\qquad\tau_X(r'\otimes(s\otimes x))=\varphi'(r')b(s)\otimes(1\otimes x).$$
For every $R$-complexes $P,J$, $S$-complex $N$, $S'$-complex $N'$, and chain maps $q:EJ\to N$, $w:BN\to N'$, $q':E'AJ\to N'$ satisfying $q'\kappa_J=wB(q)$, the following equalities of chain maps hold (composition is right to left):
$$\nu_{\varphi',AX}\tau_X=U'(\kappa_X)\mu_{EX}A(\nu_{\varphi,X}),$$
$$H_{R'}(AP,\mu_N)\chi_a(P,UN)A(\theta_{\varphi,P,N})=\theta_{\varphi',AP,BN}\,U'\bigl(H_{S'}(\kappa_P^{-1},\mathrm{id})\chi_b(EP,N)\bigr)\mu_{H_S(EP,N)},$$
$$H_{R'}(AP,\tau_J)\chi_a(P,T_\varphi J)A(\alpha_{\varphi,P,J})=\alpha_{\varphi',AP,AJ}\,T_{\varphi'}(\chi_a(P,J))\tau_{H_R(P,J)},$$
$$H_{S'}(\kappa_P^{-1},w)\chi_b(EP,N)B(\sigma^\varphi_q)=\sigma^{\varphi'}_{q'}\,E'(\chi_a(P,J))\kappa_{H_R(P,J)}.$$
Here $H(u,v)$ is the contravariant/covariant Hom action, and $H(AP,-)$ has identity first input. The maps and equations agree for identity coefficient changes and for composite coefficient squares under the iterated-extension associators $c\otimes(d\otimes x)\mapsto cd\otimes x$, whose inverses insert $1$. The same compatibility holds for any further compatible semilinear target map by its induced map $w:BN\to N'$. No flatness or boundedness is required and no Hom comparison $\chi_\psi$ is assumed invertible.

proof.text: Work on every slice and in each degree. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] the scalar extensions are sheafifications of sectionwise tensors. The generation and uniqueness clauses of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], followed by the unique factorization in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], allow us to construct linear sheaf maps from balanced formulas and test their equality on these generators. For an iterated tensor apply this argument first to the inner tensor and its sheafification, with the outer scalar fixed, and then to the outer tensor and its sheafification. For Hom-valued maps test every product coordinate [def-pur-hom-complex]; a coordinate is a map on the slice [def-pur-sheaf-hom], so test it over every object of that slice. Consequently the calculations below use arbitrary local homogeneous families, not finite-support families, and never identify a sheaf tensor's sections with the sectionwise tensor.

proof.text:
Construct the displayed formulas for $\kappa_X$ and its proposed inverse by successive tensor linearization and sheafification [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Additivity is immediate. The outer $S$-balance for $\kappa$ is $s'b(t)b(s)=s'b(ts)$; its inner $R$-balance is
$$s'b(s)b\varphi(r)\otimes(1\otimes x)=s'b(s)\varphi'a(r)\otimes(1\otimes x)=s'b(s)\otimes(1\otimes rx).$$
For the inverse, outer $R'$-balance is multiplication by $\varphi'(t')$; inner $R$-balance is the same equality $b\varphi(r)=\varphi'a(r)$ in reverse. Thus the two formulas define $S'$-linear maps. Their composites are
$$s'\otimes(s\otimes x)\longmapsto s'b(s)\otimes(1\otimes x)=s'\otimes(s\otimes x),$$
$$s'\otimes(r'\otimes x)\longmapsto s'\varphi'(r')\otimes(1\otimes x)=s'\otimes(r'\otimes x).$$
Step 1 promotes these to inverse sheaf maps. Replacing $x$ by $d_Xx$ on either side gives the chain equation; replacing it by $h(x)$ gives naturality for every chain map $h$. Restriction of sections preserves every formula, since the coefficient arrows are sheaf maps. This constructs the natural chain isomorphism $\kappa$.

proof.text:
For $\mu_N$, the $R$-balance is
$$\varphi'(r'a(r))\otimes z=\varphi'(r')b\varphi(r)\otimes z=\varphi'(r')\otimes\varphi(r)z.$$
The formula is $R'$-linear when the target action is through $\varphi'$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For $\tau_X$, inner $R$-balance follows from $b\varphi=\varphi'a$; outer $R$-balance follows from the same equality, and $R'$-linearity follows from the target's $\varphi'$-action. Explicitly the relation $r'a(r)\otimes(s\otimes x)=r'\otimes(\varphi(r)s\otimes x)$ gives the common image $\varphi'(r')b(s)b\varphi(r)\otimes(1\otimes x)$; the inner relation moves $b\varphi(r)=\varphi'a(r)$ to $1\otimes rx$ in $AX$. Tensor linearization and sheafification [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] therefore give $\mu,\tau$. Their formulas commute with restriction, with $d_N$ or $d_X$, and with a map of the last variable, by applying that map to $z$ or $x$. Hence these are natural chain maps.

proof.text:
For the first equation, apply both composites to $r'\otimes(s\otimes x)$. The normalization of $\nu$ [lem-sfb-slice-scalar-hom-chain-adjunction], and the formulas for $\mu,\kappa,\tau$ in steps 2–3, give on both sides
$$\varphi'(r')b(s)\otimes(1\otimes x)\quad\text{in }U'E'AX.$$
The nested tensor uniqueness of step 1 [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] proves the equation in every degree, hence as chain maps.

proof.text:
For the $\theta$ equation, take $r'\otimes g$ with $g$ a degree-$n$ section of $H_S(EP,N)$, and evaluate coordinate $i$ at $r''\otimes p$ in $AP^i$. The normalizations [lem-sfb-slice-scalar-hom-chain-adjunction] [lem-sfb-scalar-hom-chain-evaluation] give on the left $\mu_N(r'r''\otimes g^i(1\otimes p))$, namely
$$\varphi'(r'r'')\otimes g^i(1\otimes p).$$
On the right, $\mu$ first gives $\varphi'(r')\otimes g$; $\theta_{\varphi'}$ evaluates at $1\otimes(r''\otimes p)$, which $\kappa_P^{-1}$ sends to $\varphi'(r'')\otimes(1\otimes p)$. The $\chi_b$ formula gives the same value. This calculation is on every further slice, so product-coordinate equality [def-pur-hom-complex] and the tensor/sheafification uniqueness of step 1 prove exactly the second displayed equation, with the contravariant Hom input $\kappa_P^{-1}$.

proof.text:
For the $\alpha$ equation, take $r'\otimes(s\otimes f)$ with $f$ of degree $n$ and evaluate coordinate $i$ at $r''\otimes p$. By [lem-sfb-scalar-hom-chain-evaluation], the left side first gives $r'r''\otimes(s\otimes f^i(p))$ and then
$$\varphi'(r'r'')b(s)\otimes(1\otimes f^i(p)).$$
On the right, $\tau$ gives $\varphi'(r')b(s)\otimes(1\otimes f)$, and $\chi_a(1\otimes f)$ sends $r''\otimes p$ to $r''\otimes f^i(p)$. Applying $\alpha_{\varphi'}$ therefore gives $\varphi'(r')b(s)\otimes(r''\otimes f^i(p))$, equal to the preceding expression by $R'$-balance [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Equality on every slice and coordinate [def-pur-hom-complex], then step 1, gives the third equation.

proof.text:
For the $\sigma$ equation, use $s'\otimes(s\otimes f)$ in $BEH_R(P,J)^n$ and evaluate coordinate $i$ at $t'\otimes(r''\otimes p)$ in $E'AP^i$. The formulas of [lem-sfb-scalar-hom-chain-evaluation] and step 2 give for the left composite
$$s't'\varphi'(r'')b(s)\,w(1\otimes q(1\otimes f^i(p))).$$
Indeed $\kappa_P^{-1}$ sends that argument to $t'\varphi'(r'')\otimes(1\otimes p)$, and $B(\sigma_q)$ followed by $\chi_b$ evaluates it as $s't'\varphi'(r'')\otimes s q(1\otimes f^i(p))$ before applying $w$. On the right, $\kappa_{H_R(P,J)}$ gives $s'b(s)\otimes(1\otimes f)$ and $E'(\chi_a)$ gives $s'b(s)\otimes F$, where $F^i(r''\otimes p)=r''\otimes f^i(p)$. Thus $\sigma^{\varphi'}_{q'}$ gives
$$s'b(s)t'\varphi'(r'')\,q'(1\otimes(1\otimes f^i(p))).$$
The assumed equality $q'\kappa_J=wB(q)$, applied to $1\otimes(1\otimes f^i(p))$ in $BEJ$, identifies the last factor with $w(1\otimes q(1\otimes f^i(p)))$. The scalars commute. Product coordinates [def-pur-hom-complex] and step 1 finish the fourth equation for arbitrary $q',w$, not just scalar-extended $q$.

proof.text:
For successive ring maps $u:K\to L$, $v:L\to M$, construct the extension associator by
$$m\otimes(l\otimes x)\longmapsto m v(l)\otimes x,\qquad m\otimes x\longmapsto m\otimes(1\otimes x).$$
Both are balanced, and their composites are the identity by the same relation $m v(l)\otimes y=m\otimes ly$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. They descend uniquely [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], commute with differentials and are natural by substitution in $x$. On three successive extensions, both contractions send $n\otimes(m\otimes(l\otimes x))$ to $n w(m)w v(l)\otimes x$, for $w:M\to N$; thus associativity of multiplication proves coherence. For the identity ring map use $k\otimes x\mapsto kx$, inverse $x\mapsto1\otimes x$; its two unit equations follow from $1\otimes kx=k\otimes x$. These prove the specified associators and unit identifications without a separate associativity theorem.

proof.text:
Add a second square $c:R'\to R''$, $d:S'\to S''$, $\varphi'':R''\to S''$ with $d\varphi'=\varphi''c$; put $C=E_c,D=E_d$. Compare the maps of the composite square $(ca,db)$ with the two successive squares, using step 8. For $\kappa$, both paths on $s''\otimes(s'\otimes(s\otimes x))$ give
$$s''d(s')db(s)\otimes(1\otimes(1\otimes x)),$$
where direct contraction uses $d(s'b(s))=d(s')db(s)$. For $\mu$, both paths on $r''\otimes(r'\otimes z)$ give
$$\varphi''(r''c(r'))\otimes z,$$
since the successive path contracts $\varphi''(r'')\otimes(\varphi'(r')\otimes z)$ and $d\varphi'=\varphi''c$. For $\tau$, both paths on $r''\otimes(r'\otimes(s\otimes x))$ give
$$\varphi''(r''c(r'))db(s)\otimes(1\otimes(1\otimes x)).$$
Here the successive scalar is $\varphi''(r'')d(\varphi'(r')b(s))$, which is exactly the displayed scalar. Tensor uniqueness [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and sheafification uniqueness [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] extend these identities. If $a,b$ are identities, $\kappa,\mu,\tau$ become the identity after the unit identifications, by the same formulas. This proves identity and composite compatibility for the new comparison maps.

proof.text:
The supplied normalizations also respect these associators. For $u:K\to L$, $v:L\to M$ as in step 8, write a scalar-extension Hom generator as $m\otimes(l\otimes f)$ and an extended source generator as $t\otimes(s\otimes p)$. The successive $\chi_v E_v(\chi_u)$, contracted in its target, evaluates to $mt\,v(ls)\otimes f^i(p)$. Direct $\chi_{vu}$ evaluates the contracted inputs $mv(l)\otimes f$, $tv(s)\otimes p$ to the same element, by [lem-sfb-scalar-hom-chain-evaluation]. Successive $\theta$ evaluates a Hom family at $1\otimes(1\otimes p)$, which contracts to $1\otimes p$, the direct $\theta$ value [lem-sfb-slice-scalar-hom-chain-adjunction]. Successive $\alpha$ gives $m\otimes(l\otimes f^i(p))$, contracting to $mv(l)\otimes f^i(p)$; $\nu$ leaves this tensor unchanged. For $\sigma$, with $q:E_uJ\to N$, $w:E_vN\to N'$ and $q_{vu}=wE_v(q)$ after the associator, both successive and direct evaluation give
$$mt\,v(ls)\,w(1\otimes q(1\otimes f^i(p))).$$
Thus all four normalizations compose, and for identity ring maps they reduce to evaluation at $p$, the identity on Hom, and postcomposition by $q$. Step 9 identifies the comparison maps in two stacked squares; the four equations in steps 4–7 can therefore be pasted, with adjacent Hom actions composed componentwise [def-pur-hom-complex], to give the equations for their composite. The just-computed normalization formulas identify their pasted boundaries with the direct boundaries. All equalities are tested by step 1. Induction on the number of squares gives every finite tower.

proof.text: Finally a compatible $b$-semilinear chain map $h:N\to N'$ induces $w:BN\to N'$ by $w(s'\otimes z)=s'h(z)$: the balance is $s'b(s)\,h(z)=s'h(sz)$ and it commutes with differentials. The tensor and sheafification universal properties [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] give this map without any surjectivity or flatness hypothesis. Step 7 already allowed precisely this arbitrary $w$, subject only to $q'\kappa_J=wB(q)$. For a further semilinear map the induced composite is $w_2E_d(w)$ after step 8, as both send $s''\otimes(s'\otimes z)$ to $s''d(s')h_2(h(z))$. Consequently step 10 applies to these target changes too. Every argument is degreewise and uses all Hom coordinates, so boundedness, product preservation by scalar extension, and invertibility of $\chi$ were never needed.
